2608.00821.title: Exemplars in Disguise: Pure Exemplar Models Mimic Abstraction-First Learning
2608.00821.paper_summary: Whether idiosyncratic, item-specific knowledge is learned before abstract class-level generalizations, or vice versa, is a central question in language learning, with exemplar and abstraction-based theories making opposite predictions. Recent methods have claimed to show that, at least for large language models, abstract knowledge is learned first. We show that these methods fall short: pure memorizer models with no abstract representations can appear, by the same criteria, to learn either item-specific or class-level knowledge first, depending on their sensitivity to individual observations, with the transition point governed by the distributional properties of the input. We further argue that the distinction between item-specific and abstract knowledge may be ill-defined for distributed representations, as a word's class-level properties may not be separable from its item-specific properties.
2608.00821.paper_summary_zh: 無論是特異的、針對項目的知識在抽象的類別層級概括之前學習，還是相反，都是語言學習中的一個核心問題，具體例子和基於抽象的理論做出了相反的預測。<lb/>最近的方法聲稱顯示，至少對於大型語言模型來說，抽象知識是首先學習的。<lb/>我們顯示這些方法的不足之處：純粹的記憶模型沒有抽象表徵，根據相同的標準，似乎可以先學習特定項目或類別層級的知識，這取決於它們對個別觀察的敏感性，轉折點由輸入的分佈特性所決定。<lb/>我們進一步主張，對於分佈式表徵而言，特定項目知識和抽象知識之間的區別可能是模糊不清的，因為一個詞的類別層級特性可能無法與其特定項目特性分開。
2608.00821.author: Zachary Nicholas Houghton et.al.
